entities.summary: Robert de Pontigny, O.Cist., was a French monk, abbot, and Roman Catholic Cardinal who played a crucial role in the governance of the Catholic Church during the 14th century. Born in the 13th century, de Pontigny rose to prominence as the Abbot of the Cistercian monastery in Pontigny, France, and later became the Cardinal-Priest of the Basilica of San Pietro in Vaticano. His influence extended beyond the Catholic Church, with de Pontigny contributing to the development of the University of Paris, one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in Europe. De Pontigny's legacy can be seen in the numerous architectural and artistic projects he commissioned, including the construction of the Pontigny Abbey Church, which still stands today. His impact on the Catholic Church and European society during this period is a testament to his enduring influence.
